entities.name: Human organism
entities.description: The whole human body, considered as one integrated system of interacting organ systems across the lifespan.

entities.name: Nervous system
entities.description: The brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves, responsible for sensing, processing, and coordinating responses throughout the body.

entities.name: Cardiovascular system
entities.description: The heart and blood vessels, which circulate blood, oxygen, nutrients and signalling molecules throughout the body.

entities.name: Respiratory system
entities.description: The airways and lungs, which exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood.

entities.name: Musculoskeletal system
entities.description: Skeletal muscle, bone, cartilage, tendon and ligament, providing structure, movement and metabolic reserve.

entities.name: Immune system
entities.description: The cells, tissues and signalling networks that defend against infection and maintain tissue homeostasis.

entities.name: Endocrine system
entities.description: Hormone-secreting glands that regulate growth, metabolism, reproduction and stress responses across tissues.

entities.name: Metabolic system
entities.description: The liver, pancreas, adipose tissue and associated signalling that manage energy storage, release and nutrient handling.

entities.name: Renal system
entities.description: The kidneys and urinary tract, which filter blood, regulate fluid and electrolyte balance, and clear waste.

entities.name: Gastrointestinal system
entities.description: The digestive tract and its resident microbial ecosystem, handling digestion, absorption and barrier function.

entities.name: Reproductive system
entities.description: The organs and hormonal axes governing reproduction, which undergo distinctive and sex-specific age-associated change.

entities.name: Skin
entities.description: The skin and associated structures, forming the barrier between the body and its environment.

entities.name: Sensory systems
entities.description: The eyes, ears and other sensory organs that transduce environmental signals into neural activity.

entities.name: Brain
entities.description: The central organ of the nervous system, showing regionally varied age-associated change in volume, connectivity and vascular supply.

entities.name: Spinal cord
entities.description: The neural pathway connecting brain and peripheral nerves.

entities.name: Heart
entities.description: The muscular pump that circulates blood; shows age-associated changes in wall thickness, filling and rhythm.

entities.name: Arteries
entities.description: Vessels carrying blood away from the heart; arterial stiffening is among the better-characterised age-associated changes.

entities.name: Lungs
entities.description: Paired organs of gas exchange, showing age-associated change in elastic recoil and alveolar surface.

entities.name: Skeletal muscle
entities.description: Voluntary muscle tissue; mass and strength decline with age, with strength typically declining faster than mass.

entities.name: Bone
entities.description: Mineralised connective tissue undergoing continuous remodelling, whose balance shifts with age and hormonal status.

entities.name: Thymus
entities.description: The organ in which T cells mature; it involutes progressively from early life onward.

entities.name: Bone marrow
entities.description: The site of blood and immune cell production, housing haematopoietic stem cells.

entities.name: Liver
entities.description: The principal organ of metabolic processing, detoxification and protein synthesis.

entities.name: Pancreas
entities.description: Source of digestive enzymes and of the hormones regulating blood glucose.

entities.name: Kidneys
entities.description: Paired filtering organs; nephron number and filtration capacity decline with age.

entities.name: Intestines
entities.description: The absorptive tract and principal site of the gut microbial ecosystem.

entities.name: Skin tissue
entities.description: The layered barrier organ, showing age-associated change in thickness, elasticity and repair capacity.

entities.name: Eyes
entities.description: Sensory organs of vision, where lens proteins accumulate damage over decades.

entities.name: Cardiac tissue
entities.description: The contractile and connective tissue of the heart wall.

entities.name: Arterial wall
entities.description: The layered vessel wall whose elastin and collagen composition changes with age.

entities.name: Skeletal muscle tissue
entities.description: Bundled muscle fibres with their satellite-cell niche and connective scaffold.

entities.name: Trabecular bone
entities.description: The internal lattice of bone, more metabolically active than cortical bone.

entities.name: Gut epithelium
entities.description: The rapidly renewing absorptive lining of the intestine.

entities.name: Cardiomyocyte
entities.description: The contractile cell of cardiac muscle, largely post-mitotic in adults and heavily dependent on mitochondrial energy supply.

entities.name: Muscle satellite cell
entities.description: The resident muscle stem cell responsible for repair and regeneration of muscle fibres.

entities.name: Fibroblast
entities.description: A connective-tissue cell producing extracellular matrix; the cell type in which replicative limits were first described.

entities.name: Haematopoietic stem cell
entities.description: The blood-forming stem cell, which shows age-associated lineage bias and reduced regenerative output.

entities.name: T cell
entities.description: An adaptive immune cell whose naive population contracts as the thymus involutes.

entities.name: Neuron
entities.description: The signalling cell of the nervous system, long-lived and dependent on proteostasis and mitochondrial quality control.

entities.name: Mitochondria
entities.description: Organelles generating most cellular ATP and acting as hubs for metabolic and stress signalling.

entities.name: Lysosome
entities.description: The degradative organelle that receives and breaks down material delivered by autophagy.

entities.name: Nucleus
entities.description: The organelle housing genomic DNA and its chromatin organisation.

entities.name: mTOR signalling
entities.description: A nutrient-sensing pathway coupling amino-acid and growth-factor availability to protein synthesis and autophagy.

entities.name: AMPK signalling
entities.description: An energy-sensing pathway activated by low cellular energy that promotes catabolism and autophagy.

entities.name: Insulin/IGF-1 signalling
entities.description: A conserved growth and nutrient pathway whose reduction extends lifespan in several model organisms.

entities.name: DNA damage response
entities.description: The network detecting and repairing DNA lesions, which can trigger senescence when damage is persistent.

entities.name: Senescence-associated secretory phenotype
entities.description: The pro-inflammatory secretory programme of senescent cells, affecting neighbouring tissue.

entities.name: Macroautophagy pathway
entities.description: The pathway sequestering damaged components for lysosomal degradation and recycling.

entities.name: Leukocyte telomere length
entities.description: Telomere length measured in circulating white blood cells; a widely used but imperfect proxy for telomere state elsewhere.

entities.name: DNA methylation age
entities.description: An age predictor built from methylation at selected CpG sites; predicts chronological age well, but is not a validated measure of an individual's functional state.

entities.name: Interleukin-6
entities.description: A circulating inflammatory cytokine commonly elevated in older adults and associated with frailty outcomes.

entities.name: p16INK4a-positive cell burden
entities.description: A marker used to estimate senescent-cell load in tissue; no single marker is universally reliable.

entities.name: Grip strength
entities.description: A simple functional measure of muscle strength used in sarcopenia assessment.

entities.name: Estimated glomerular filtration rate
entities.description: An estimate of kidney filtering capacity derived from serum markers.

entities.name: Gut microbiome uniqueness
entities.description: A measure of how distinct an individual's gut microbial profile is relative to a reference population.
